section: Chapter Two — Forbidden Items and Seclusion
subtitle: Libation wine, forbidden foods, seclusion laws, and bathing with idolaters
author: Moses Maimonides
intro: Rambam's commentary on Tractate Avodah Zarah — the laws of idolatry, forbidden commercial dealings, libation wine, and the nullification of idols. Original 12th-century Judeo-Arabic with English translation.

aligned.ja: משנה [א]
aligned.en: Mishnah [1]

aligned.ja: ולו בהמה נקבה לא תתרך ענד גויה ללא יגי גוי לתלך אלגויה פינכח אלבהימה.
aligned.en: The prohibition against leaving a female animal alone with an idolater[^1] applies because a [male] idolater might come to that idolatress woman and copulate with the animal.

pairs.ja: בהמה נקבה לא תתרך ענד גויה
pairs.en: leaving a female animal alone with an idolater

fn.1: JA *goyah* — an idolatress, i.e., a non-Jewish woman. The concern throughout M1 is mingling that could lead either to sexual transgression or to enabling idolatry.

aligned.ja: וקולה לא תתיחד אשה עמהן, ולו אליחוד אלד'י יחל להא מת'לה מע ישראל מת'ל אן תכון זוג'הֵ אלגוי מעה ונחו ד'לך ממא בינא פי מוצ'עה פי אכ'ר קדושין.
aligned.en: As for the statement, "A woman may not be secluded with them" — even the seclusion that would be permissible for her with a Jewish man is forbidden here, for example when an idolater's wife is present with him, and similar situations, as we have explained in its proper place at the end of tractate Kiddushin.

pairs.en: A woman may not be secluded with them

pairs.en: the seclusion that would be permissible for her with a Jewish man

pairs.en: we have explained in its proper place at the end of tractate Kiddushin

aligned.ja: ובת ישראל לא תילד את הנכרית, לאנהא תרבי ולד לעבודה זרה. ואן כאן בשכר מותר משום איבה.
aligned.en: A Jewish woman may not serve as midwife for an idolatress, because she would thereby be raising a child for idolatry. If it is done for payment, however, it is permitted on account of enmity.[^2]

pairs.ja: בת ישראל לא תילד את הנכרית
pairs.en: A Jewish woman may not serve as midwife for an idolatress

pairs.ja: תרבי ולד לעבודה זרה
pairs.en: raising a child for idolatry

pairs.ja: אן כאן בשכר מותר משום איבה
pairs.en: done for payment, however, it is permitted on account of enmity

fn.2: Heb. *mishum eivah* — a recognized Rabbinic principle permitting certain otherwise-prohibited acts with non-Jews where refusal would provoke hostility dangerous to the Jewish community.

aligned.ja: ומן הד'ה אלעלה לא תניק בנה של נכרית. וקולה ברשותה, לאנהא לא תפרד מעה לאנהם חשודין על שפיכת דמים.
aligned.en: For this same reason, [a Jewish woman] may not nurse the infant of an idolatress. The phrase "in her domain" [applies] because [the Jewish woman] may not be alone with him [the idolater], since idolaters are suspect regarding bloodshed.[^3]

pairs.en: in her domain

pairs.en: may not be alone with him

pairs.en: idolaters are suspect regarding bloodshed

fn.3: JA *shafikh dam* (Heb. *shefikhut damim*). The Talmud (BT AZ 25b–26a) identifies idolaters as suspect in this regard, hence the rule that a Jewish woman may not be secluded with an idolater.

aligned.en: Mishnah [2]

aligned.ja: רפוי ממון, אן יטב לה דאבתה או עבידה אלגוים. ורפוי נפשות, טב נפסה.
aligned.en: "Healing of property" means treating his animal or his idolater-owned slaves.[^4] "Healing of persons" means treating the idolater himself.

fn.4: The Mishnah distinguishes "healing of property" (*refu'at mamonot*) from "healing of persons" (*refu'at nefashot*). Rambam clarifies that "healing of property" extends to the idolater's own slaves, not only his livestock.

aligned.ja: והד'א אד'א דפע לה אלדוא מן ענד נפסה אמא אד'א אחאלה עלי מא יעמל פחלאל, ולד'לך יג'וז אלפתוי ואכ'ד' אלנסך' מנהם ולא יג'וז שרא אלמעאנאה מנהם.
aligned.en: This applies when the physician administers the remedy from his own hand. If, however, he refers the patient to something the patient himself prepares, it is permitted. For this reason it is permissible to write out a prescription (*nusḵa*)[^5] for them and to accept remuneration from them, but it is not permissible to sell them direct medical treatment.

aligned.en: Mishnah [3]

aligned.ja: כאן אדריאנוס קיסר אלמלך קד אתכ'ד' טינא מעלום ועג'נה באלכ'מר מדה מן אלזמאן ת'ם עמל מנה כ'זף גיר מטבוך', וכאן ינקלה מע נפסה, פחית' מא אראד אלשרב אנקע שקפא מן ד'לך אלכ'זף פי אלמא פירסב אלטין ויבקי אלמא ממזוג' באלכ'מר פישרבה.
aligned.en: The Emperor Hadrian had taken a known quantity of clay, kneaded it with wine for a period of time, then formed from it an unfired ceramic vessel, which he would carry with him. Whenever he wished to drink, he would soak a shard of that ceramic in water; the clay would settle and the water, infused with wine, would remain, and he would drink it.

pairs.en: soak a shard of that ceramic in water

pairs.en: the clay would settle and the water, infused with wine, would remain, and he would drink it

aligned.ja: ובקית תלך אלצנאעה באידי אלנאס ענד תדוין אלמשנה והו חרם אדריאני מנסוב לאדריאנוס.
aligned.en: That craft persisted in people's hands at the time the Mishnah was compiled, and it is called the "Hadrianic [vessel]" (*ḥerem Adriani*), named after Hadrian.[^6]

fn.6: The "Hadrianic vessel" (*ḥerem Adriani* / *ḥurmei shel Adrianus*) — an unusual ceramic infused with wine during manufacture. Rambam explains this as an artifact of a specific Roman practice that had become widespread by Mishnaic times.

aligned.ja: ולבובין, מאכ'וד' מן לב, לאנהם כאנוא ית'קבון עלי קלובהא ויכ'רג'והא והי נוע מן עבאדהֵ אלמעאבד. ותרפות, אלנקץ ואלהואן. ומקום התורפה יסמון אלמוצ'ע אלמסתהאן אלמחתקר, והי עבארה ען ביות אלמעאבד אלתי יחג' להא, ולד'לך סמי אלחג'אג' ההולכין בתרפות.
aligned.en: "Lubbin" (*lubbin*) derives from the word *lev* (heart), because [the idolaters] would pierce [the image] at its heart and extract it — this being a type of sacrifice performed in the temples. "Tarpot" (*tarpot*) means ruin and degradation. The expression *mekom ha-tarpeh* designates a place of disgrace and contempt, referring to those pilgrimage shrines to which people make pilgrimage — hence the pilgrims who travel *be-tarpot* are so called.

aligned.ja: והבאין מותרין אד'א ג'אוא פראדא, אמא אד'א כאנת קאפלה אסורין שמא דעתן לחזור. והלכה כרבן שמעון בן גמליאל. וכר' עקיבה.
aligned.en: Those returning [from such places] are permitted if they come individually; if they come in a caravan, they are forbidden, lest their intention be to return. The ruling follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and Rabbi Akiva.

aligned.en: Mishnah [4]

aligned.ja: חכם נאדות הגוים וקנקניהם עלי מא אצף, אן כאנת ג'דידה לם תסתכ'דם פי מא יבדוא לאלעין פיג'וז לנא אן נג'על פיהא אלכ'מר מן אול אלאמר, ואן כאנת באליה קד אסתכ'דמת פיקצרהא פי אלמא ת'לאת'ה איאם מן אלוקת לאלוקת ויבדל ענהא אלמא כל ארבע ועשרין סאעה ויעמל פיהא אלכ'מר בעד ד'לך.
aligned.en: The Sage's ruling on wineskins (*nodot*)[^7] and jugs (*kankanim*) of idolaters is as follows. If they are new and have never apparently been used, we may fill them with wine from the outset. If they are old and have been used, one must soak them in water for three full days, changing the water every twenty-four hours; after that one may use them for wine.

pairs.ja: נאדות הגוים וקנקניהם
pairs.en: wineskins and jugs of idolaters

pairs.ja: ג'דידה לם תסתכ'דם
pairs.en: new and have never apparently been used

pairs.ja: נג'על פיהא אלכ'מר מן אול אלאמר
pairs.en: fill them with wine from the outset

pairs.ja: פיקצרהא פי אלמא ת'לאת'ה איאם
pairs.en: soak them in water for three full days

pairs.ja: ויבדל ענהא אלמא כל ארבע ועשרין סאעה
pairs.en: changing the water every twenty-four hours

fn.7: Heb. *nodot* — leather wineskins, as distinguished from ceramic or clay jars. The concern is absorption of libation wine (*yayin nesekh*) into the porous material.

aligned.ja: ואן ג'על פיהא דון אן יקצרהא באלמא ציר או מרי או נחוהמא פיג'וז לה אן יג'על פיהא בעד ד'לך אלכ'מר. ויג'וז לה אן יג'על פיהא שכר לכתחלה. וכד'לך אן אחמאהא באלנאר יג'וז לה אן יג'על פיהא אלכ'מר.
aligned.en: If, without soaking in water, one placed vinegar, brine (*muri*), or the like in them, one may subsequently use them for wine. It is permissible to put beer in them from the outset. Likewise, if one heated them with fire, one may subsequently put wine in them.

pairs.en: placed vinegar, brine, or the like in them

pairs.ja: פיג'וז לה אן יג'על פיהא בעד ד'לך אלכ'מר
pairs.en: one may subsequently use them for wine

pairs.en: permissible to put beer in them from the outset

pairs.ja: אן אחמאהא באלנאר

aligned.ja: ואן לם יפעל פיהא שי מן הד'ה אלת'אלת'ה אלאוג'ה ובקית ענדה עאמא כאמלא פארגה פיג'וז לה אן יג'על פיהא אלכ'מר.
aligned.en: If none of these three treatments was performed, but the vessel remained in one's possession for an entire year while empty, one may put wine in it.

aligned.ja: וקד ד'כרנא מראת אן חרצנין, עג'ם אלענב. וזוגין, אלקשר אלד'י עלי אלחבה. ולחים, תתסמי טאל אלסנה. ויבשים, בעד עאם. וקול אלחכמים מותרין, ירידון בה מותרין באכילה.
aligned.en: We have mentioned on several occasions that *ḥarẓanin* means grape seeds, *zugin* the husk surrounding the berry, *laḥim* applies when [grapes are] still fresh in the current year, and *yeveshim* after one year. When the Sages say [the seeds and husks] are "permitted," they mean permitted for eating.

aligned.ja: וכאן עאדתהם אן יג'עלון אלכ'מר פי בעץ' אנואע אלמרי ולד'לך חרם באכילה. ותבין פי אלתלמוד אנה אד'א תחקקנא מן צפהֵ ד'לך אלמרי וקואמה אנה לם ידכ'לה כ'מר פהו מותר באכילה.
aligned.en: It was their custom to place wine in certain types of brine (*muri*), and for that reason [those brines] are forbidden for eating. It is clarified in the Talmud that if we are certain from the nature and consistency of a particular brine that no wine entered it, it is permitted for eating.

pairs.en: their custom to place wine in certain types of brine

aligned.ja: ובית אוניאקי, מוצ'ע כאנת מעט'ם אלעג'ול אלתי הנאך כלהא תקרב לעבודה זרה, פצאר מעט'ם תלך אלעג'ול באלאצ'אפה לג'מלהֵ אלבהאים מיעוט, ור' מאיר חייש למיעוט פלד'לך יקול ג'מלהֵ ג'בן תלך אלמדינה אסור בהנייה מן סבב קיבת עגלי עבודה זרה.
aligned.en: Beit Uniaki (*beit unyaki*)[^8] was a place where most of the calves present were offered to idolatry. Since most of those calves, relative to all the animals, formed a minority, Rabbi Meir — who is stringent regarding minorities (*miut*)[^9] — holds that the entire production of cheese from that city is forbidden to derive benefit from, on account of the rennet of idolatrous calves.

fn.8: Beit Uniaki (*beit unyaki* / *bet uniyaki*) — a specific locality whose calves were predominantly consecrated for idolatrous sacrifice. The halakhic question is whether a minority (*miut*) of forbidden rennet taints the majority.
fn.9: Heb. *ḥayesh le-miut* — Rabbi Meir's well-known principle of taking precautions against even minority occurrences of a forbidden element, as against the Sages who do not apply the same stringency.

aligned.en: The Sages, who are not stringent regarding minorities, hold that it is only forbidden to eat but not forbidden for benefit. The ruling does not follow Rabbi Meir in any of his positions.

aligned.en: Mishnah [5]

aligned.ja: אלד'י אוג'ב אן לא יעלמה בסבב חרמאנהא לקרב תלך אלגזרה דילמא אתי לזלזולי בה, ולד'לך כאנת עאדתהם מתי חרמוא שי בגזרה לא יכ'ברון בסבב תלך אלגזרה מדהֵ עאם חתי ישהר חרמאן ד'לך אלשי ויסתפיץ' ענד אלנסא ואלעואם וחיניד' יכ'בר באלעלה.
aligned.en: The reason that [the Sages] did not disclose the rationale [for the prohibition on idolaters' cheese] was the concern that if they did so at the outset, people might come to treat the prohibition lightly.[^10] For this reason their practice, whenever they prohibited something by Rabbinic decree (*gezera*), was not to state the rationale for that decree for a full year, until the prohibition of that thing had become established and had spread among women and ordinary people; only then would they disclose the reason.

pairs.en: did not disclose the rationale for the prohibition

pairs.ja: דילמא אתי לזלזולי בה
pairs.en: people might come to treat the prohibition lightly

pairs.ja: חרמוא שי בגזרה לא יכ'ברון בסבב תלך אלגזרה מדהֵ עאם
pairs.en: prohibited something by Rabbinic decree, was not to state the rationale for that decree for a full year

pairs.ja: חתי ישהר חרמאן ד'לך אלשי ויסתפיץ' ענד אלנסא ואלעואם
pairs.en: until the prohibition had become established and had spread among women and ordinary people

fn.10: Rambam offers a general sociological observation about Rabbinic legislative strategy: delaying the disclosure of a decree's rationale ensures the prohibition becomes entrenched before its reasoning is exposed to scrutiny or challenge.

aligned.ja: וסבב תחרים גבינה של גוים שמא יעמידנה בעור קיבת נבילה, לאנה איצ'א מעמיד, וקד עלם אן שחיטת הנכרי נבלה, פאד'א העמיד בעור הקיבה חרם ד'לך אלג'בן ליס מן עלהֵ בשר בחלב, לאן בשר בחלב לא יחרם אלא בנותן טעם כמא נבין פי חולין, ואנמא יחרם מן אג'ל שחיטת נכרי.
aligned.en: The actual reason for the prohibition of cheese made by idolaters is the concern that they may set it [the milk] with the skin of the stomach (*abomasum*, *kevah*)[^11] of an animal carcass (*neveilah*),[^12] since that too serves as a coagulant, and it is known that an idolater's slaughter [constitutes] neveilah. If one set [the cheese] using the stomach-skin, that cheese is forbidden — not on account of the prohibition of meat-with-milk (*basar be-ḥalav*),[^13] because meat-with-milk is forbidden only when the prohibited substance imparts a flavor,[^14] as we will explain in tractate Ḥullin; rather, it is forbidden on account of the idolater's slaughter [which constitutes neveilah].

pairs.ja: גבינה של גוים שמא יעמידנה בעור קיבת נבילה
pairs.en: prohibition of cheese made by idolaters is the concern that they may set it with the stomach-skin of an animal carcass

pairs.ja: שחיטת הנכרי נבלה
pairs.en: an idolater's slaughter constitutes neveilah

pairs.ja: בשר בחלב לא יחרם אלא בנותן טעם
pairs.en: meat-with-milk is forbidden only when the prohibited substance imparts a flavor

pairs.ja: יחרם מן אג'ל שחיטת נכרי
pairs.en: forbidden on account of the idolater's slaughter

fn.11: Heb. *or ha-kevah* — the inner lining or skin of the calf's fourth stomach (abomasum), used as a natural rennet to coagulate milk. Rambam distinguishes the stomach-skin (*or ha-kevah*) from the rennet (*anpaḥa*) itself.
fn.12: Heb. *neveilah* — an animal that died without valid ritual slaughter, rendering it a carcass and Biblically forbidden for consumption.
fn.13: Heb. *basar be-ḥalav* — the Biblical prohibition on mixing meat and milk (Exod 23:19; 34:26; Deut 14:21). Rambam clarifies that this prohibition does not apply here because the operative prohibition is the neveilah of the idolater's slaughter, not the meat-milk mixture.
fn.14: Heb. *noten taʿam* — the principle that a forbidden substance mixed into a permitted one renders the mixture forbidden only when it imparts a perceptible flavor, typically calculated at less than one-in-sixty. Rambam notes this principle does not apply where the substance is a *maʿamid*.

aligned.ja: וליס נקול פי הד'א אחד מששים לכונה מעמיד ופעל אלנבלה ט'אהר, פכאן אלגבנה כלהא נבלה, לאן אלשי אלחראם אד'א אכ'תלט מע אלחלאל וכאן פעל ד'לך אלשי אלחראם באדיא ט'אהרא ולם יתלף בקלתה ולא כ'פי פהו יחרם אלג'מיע, ולו כאן אלשי אלחראם אקל מקדאר, ולא יקאל חיניד' לא אחד מששים ולא אחד ממאה עלי נחו מא בינא פי אלת'אני מן ערלה פי קולהם כל המחמץ והמתבל וכו'.
aligned.en: Nor do we apply the principle of *aḥad mi-shishshim* (one-in-sixty)[^15] here, because the forbidden substance is a coagulant (*maʿamid*),[^16] and the action of the neveilah is visible and manifest — not nullified by its small quantity, nor hidden. For when a forbidden substance mixes with a permitted one and the action of the forbidden substance is visible and manifest — not lost through its small quantity and not concealed — it renders the entire mixture forbidden, even if the forbidden substance is of minimal quantity. In such a case one does not say "one-in-sixty" or "one-in-a-hundred," as we explained in the second [chapter] of tractate Orlah regarding the rule that "whatever leavens, seasons, [or coagulates]…" (M. Orlah 2:4).

pairs.ja: לא נקול פי הד'א אחד מששים לכונה מעמיד
pairs.en: we do not apply the principle of one-in-sixty here, because the forbidden substance is a coagulant

pairs.ja: פעל אלנבלה ט'אהר
pairs.en: the action of the neveilah is visible and manifest

pairs.ja: אלשי אלחראם אד'א אכ'תלט מע אלחלאל פהו יחרם אלג'מיע
pairs.en: a forbidden substance mixes with a permitted one it renders the entire mixture forbidden

pairs.ja: לא אחד מששים ולא אחד ממאה עלי נחו מא בינא פי אלת'אני מן ערלה
pairs.en: one does not say one-in-sixty or one-in-a-hundred, as we explained in the second chapter of tractate Orlah

fn.15: Heb. *aḥad mi-shishshim* — the standard Talmudic threshold of nullification: a forbidden substance present in less than one-sixtieth of the mixture is generally considered nullified. Rambam explains this rule is inapplicable when the forbidden substance is functional as a coagulant.
fn.16: Heb./JA *maʿamid* — a coagulating or binding agent. Rambam's rule (cited from BT AZ 35b) is that any substance that functions as a coagulant (*maʿamid*) renders the entire product forbidden regardless of quantity, because its action is visible and functional rather than merely flavor-conferring.

aligned.ja: ואלמעמיד אשד מן מחמץ ומתבל, וכד'א קאלוא הכל הולך אחר המעמיד.
aligned.en: The coagulant (*maʿamid*) is more stringent than a leavening or seasoning agent; thus the rule is stated: "Everything follows the coagulant" (BT AZ 35b).

pairs.ja: אלמעמיד אשד מן מחמץ ומתבל
pairs.en: The coagulant is more stringent than a leavening or seasoning agent

pairs.ja: הכל הולך אחר המעמיד
pairs.en: Everything follows the coagulant

aligned.ja: ואמא אנפחהֵ אלנבלה נפסהא פהי חלאל לאנהא פרשא בעלמא, אעני במנזלה אלאת'פאל ואלמואד וליסת מן ד'את אלבהימה, ולד'לך יג'וז לנא שרא אנפחהֵ אלגוים ונעקד בהא אלג'בן. וכד'לך אד'א ראינא אלגוי קד עקד אללבן באלאנפחה נפסהא יחל לנא אכל ד'לך אלג'בן.
aligned.en: As for the rennet (*anpaḥa*) of a neveilah itself — it is permitted, because it is secreted matter (*parsha be-ʿalma*),[^17] meaning it has the status of waste products and materials, not of the animal's own body, and therefore we may purchase rennet from idolaters and use it to set cheese. Likewise, if we observe an idolater setting milk with the rennet itself [without the stomach-skin], we are permitted to eat that cheese.

pairs.en: the rennet of a neveilah itself is permitted

pairs.ja: פרשא בעלמא, אעני במנזלה אלאת'פאל ואלמואד
pairs.en: secreted matter, meaning it has the status of waste products and materials

pairs.en: we may purchase rennet from idolaters and use it to set cheese

pairs.ja: ראינא אלגוי קד עקד אללבן באלאנפחה נפסהא יחל לנא אכל ד'לך אלג'בן
pairs.en: if we observe an idolater setting milk with the rennet itself, we are permitted to eat that cheese

fn.17: JA/Heb. *parsha be-ʿalma* — "merely secreted matter"; Rambam's technical phrase classifying rennet as analogous to excretions or byproducts that are not constitutive parts of the animal itself and thus lack the animal's forbidden status.

aligned.ja: ולא יפיד אלעלם פי הד'א ולא גלבהֵ אלט'ן אלא אלרויה ואלמשאהדה.
aligned.en: Knowledge or strong probability is not sufficient in this matter; only actual seeing and direct observation [suffices].

pairs.en: Knowledge or strong probability is not sufficient in this matter

pairs.ja: אלא אלרויה ואלמשאהדה
pairs.en: only actual seeing and direct observation

aligned.ja: ואלד'י אוג'ב אן לא תחרם אלגבנה מן אג'ל חלב שחלבו גוי ואין ישראל רואהו, לאן עלהֵ הד'א אלחרמאן ללא יכ'לט חלב בהמה טמאה מע ד'לך אללבן, ואלאצל ענדנא חלב בהמה טמאה אינו עומד, פלם יבק חרמאן אלא חרמאן אלנבלה כמא ד'כרוא.
aligned.en: The reason why cheese is not forbidden on account of milk milked by an idolater without a Jew watching, is that the rationale for that prohibition is lest he mix in milk from a ritually impure (*tamei*) animal. But our established principle is that the milk of a *tamei* animal does not coagulate; consequently, no prohibition remains except the prohibition arising from neveilah, as stated.

pairs.ja: לא תחרם אלגבנה מן אג'ל חלב שחלבו גוי ואין ישראל רואהו
pairs.en: cheese is not forbidden on account of milk milked by an idolater without a Jew watching

pairs.en: the milk of a tamei animal does not coagulate

pairs.en: no prohibition remains except the prohibition arising from neveilah

aligned.en: Mishnah [6]

aligned.ja: אכת'ר הד'ה אלאשיא מת'ל אלפת ואלשלקות ושבההא אנמא חרמת כי נבעד ענהם ולא נכ'אלטהם, חתי לא נמתד במכ'אלטתהם לאלתסייב פי מא יחרם והו מעני קולהם משום חתנות.
aligned.en: Most of these items — such as flat bread (*pat*), boiled foods (*shelakot*), and the like — were prohibited in order to keep us at a distance from [idolaters] and to prevent us from mixing with them, lest ongoing social intercourse lead us to transgress what is forbidden, which is the meaning of their phrase "on account of [the risk of] intermarriage" (*mishum ḥatnut*).[^18]

pairs.en: Most of these items

pairs.en: were prohibited in order to keep us at a distance from [idolaters] and to prevent us from mixing with them

pairs.en: which is the meaning of their phrase "on account of [the risk of] intermarriage" (*mishum ḥatnut*)

fn.18: Heb. *mishum ḥatnut* — "on account of intermarriage." This is the underlying rationale for a broad set of social-boundary prohibitions decreed by the Sages: by forbidding shared meals and foodstuffs, they created a barrier against the social familiarity that could lead to prohibited intermarriage.

aligned.ja: והד'ה אלאשיא הי מן ג'מלהֵ שמונה עשר דבר שגזרו כמא בינא פי אול שבת.
aligned.en: These items are among the eighteen things decreed, as we have explained at the beginning of tractate Shabbat.

pairs.ja: כמא בינא פי אול שבת
pairs.en: as we have explained at the beginning of tractate Shabbat

aligned.ja: והד'א אלד'י תראנא נחרם שלוקיהם ליס הי אלאשיא אלתי יטבכ'ון פי אואניהם לאן ד'לך יתסמי גיעולי גוים, ואנמא הי אלאשיא אלתי ליס פיהא גיעולי גוים ולא שכהא, לכן תחרם מן אג'ל דבר שנגמרה מלאכתו על ידי גוי.
aligned.en: What we have stated as forbidden regarding their boiled foods is not the same things that they cook in their pots — for that category is called *giʿulei goyim* (prohibited residues of idolaters' vessels).[^19] Rather, these are foods that involve no *giʿulei goyim* issue whatsoever, yet are forbidden on account of their being "finished through the agency of an idolater" (*davar she-nigmera melakhto al yedei goy*).

pairs.ja: אלד'י תראנא נחרם שלוקיהם ליס הי אלאשיא אלתי יטבכ'ון פי אואניהם
pairs.en: What we have stated as forbidden regarding their boiled foods is not the same things that they cook in their pots

pairs.ja: לאן ד'לך יתסמי גיעולי גוים
pairs.en: for that category is called *giʿulei goyim*

pairs.ja: ואנמא הי אלאשיא אלתי ליס פיהא גיעולי גוים ולא שכהא
pairs.en: Rather, these are foods that involve no *giʿulei goyim* issue whatsoever

pairs.en: yet are forbidden on account of their being "finished through the agency of an idolater"

fn.19: Heb. *giʿulei goyim* — literally "the abominations of idolaters"; technically, the forbidden residues absorbed into an idolater's cooking vessels that may leach into Jewish food cooked therein. Rambam carefully distinguishes this from *bishul akum*.

aligned.ja: לאן אלחכמים חרמוא מן אג'ל אלבעד ענהם איצ'א כל מא יטבכ'ה אלגוי ולו טבך' שינא פי חכמנא, אלא אן יכון ד'לך אלשי נאכל כמות שהוא חי, או אינו עולה על שלחן מלכים לאכול בו את הפת פי ד'לך אלמוצ'ע, פאנה לא יחרם אד'א טבכ'ה אלגוי משום בשולי גוים.
aligned.en: For the Sages prohibited, in order to keep distance from them, anything that an idolater cooks, even if he cooked it in our [Jewish-owned] vessels — unless the item can be eaten raw, or [unless it is something that] does not appear on a king's table to be eaten with bread in that locale. In such cases it is not forbidden when an idolater cooks it under the rubric of *bishul akum*.[^20]

pairs.ja: אלחכמים חרמוא מן אג'ל אלבעד ענהם כל מא יטבכ'ה אלגוי
pairs.en: the Sages prohibited, in order to keep distance from them, anything that an idolater cooks

pairs.ja: אלא אן יכון ד'לך אלשי נאכל כמות שהוא חי
pairs.en: unless the item can be eaten raw

pairs.ja: או אינו עולה על שלחן מלכים לאכול בו את הפת
pairs.en: or [unless it is something that] does not appear on a king's table to be eaten with bread

pairs.ja: פאנה לא יחרם אד'א טבכ'ה אלגוי משום בשולי גוים
pairs.en: it is not forbidden when an idolater cooks it under the rubric of *bishul akum*

fn.20: Heb. *bishul akum* — "cooking by an idolater" (or non-Jew); a Rabbinic prohibition on food cooked by a non-Jew even in Jewish vessels. Rambam's two exemptions — food eaten raw, and food not served at a royal table — are the standard Talmudic criteria (BT AZ 38a).

aligned.ja: ולא יכ'תלט עליך חרמאן בשולי גוים בחרמאן גיעולי גוים וקד בינת לך ד'לך.
aligned.en: Do not confuse the prohibition of *bishul akum* with the prohibition of *giʿulei goyim*; I have made that distinction clear for you.

pairs.ja: ולא יכ'תלט עליך חרמאן בשולי גוים בחרמאן גיעולי גוים
pairs.en: Do not confuse the prohibition of *bishul akum* with the prohibition of *giʿulei goyim*

aligned.ja: ואמא אלזית פקטוע אלהלכה אן זית גוים חלאל וכ'בזהם יבדוא מן תלמודנא אלבבלי אנה חראם, לכן כ'בז אלסוק אלד'י יביע באיעהֵ אלכ'בז אקל חרמאן ואקרב לאלחלאל מן כ'בז אלדיאר, ופי אלאספאר וענד אלצ'ראיר יחל, ואלאמר ענדי פיה ראג'ע למנהג המדינה כמא בינת פי פסחים.
aligned.en: As for olive oil: the established ruling is that oil of idolaters is permitted. Bread of idolaters (*pat akum*)[^21] appears from our Babylonian Talmud to be forbidden, yet market bread (*pat ha-suk*) — sold by a bread-vendor — is less forbidden and closer to permitted than household bread; in traveling and in times of pressing need it is permitted. In my view, the matter ultimately follows local custom, as I have explained in tractate Pesaḥim.

pairs.en: the established ruling is that oil of idolaters is permitted

fn.21: Heb. *pat akum* (or *pat nakhri*) — bread baked by a non-Jew. Rambam distinguishes commercial (*pat ha-suk*) from domestic (*pat ha-bayit*) non-Jewish bread, citing greater leniency for the former and complete leniency in cases of necessity or travel.

aligned.ja: ולם תחרם אלמכבסאת אלתי יג'עלון פיהא אלכ'מר בהנאה לאנהא לא יט'הר פיהא פעל אלכ'מר בל יתלאשא, ויתלף מטעמה, פלד'לך לא תחרם בהנאה.
aligned.en: Pickled foods (*mekavsot*) that contain wine are not forbidden for benefit, because the action of the wine is not apparent in them but rather dissipates and its flavor is destroyed; therefore they are not forbidden for benefit.

pairs.en: therefore they are not forbidden for benefit

aligned.ja: וטרית, נוע מן אנואע אלסמך והו דג טהור, כאנוא ידקונה חתי יציר כאלעג'ין ויאכלון בה, פאד'א דק ודרס חרמנאה כ'שיתנא אן יכון קד דק מעה דג טמא וליס ת'ם צורה יסתדל בהא.
aligned.en: *Tarit*[^22] is a type of clean fish that they would pound until it became paste-like and eat. Once pounded and pressed, we forbade it lest an impure (*tamei*) fish was pounded along with it and there is no visible form by which to identify it.

pairs.en: *Tarit* is a type of clean fish

pairs.ja: וליס ת'ם צורה יסתדל בהא
pairs.en: there is no visible form by which to identify it

fn.22: Heb. *tarit* — a type of clean fish, ground into a paste. Because it loses its identifying features when ground, one cannot verify it is free of forbidden fish species.

aligned.ja: וציר, הו מרק אלסמך אלממלח אלד'י ימצל מנה, פאד'א לם יכון פיה סמך לא נעלם הל מן דג טמא מצל או מן דג טהור ולד'לך יחרם.
